hook: Stop writing code, and your reviews get worse

beats.say: A new essay argues that developers who hand all their coding to AI agents and only review the output are slowly losing their craft.
The author compares it to a guitarist who stops practicing and only directs other players, or a writer who only reads and critiques mostly AI-generated prose.
His point isn't the short-term quality of agent output. It's that in every other field, skills decay without practice, and reviewing code well depends on actually writing it.
